message.content:
Keysight Technologies Inc closed the quarter ended on 2026-07-31 with revenue of 1.85 billion and earnings per share of 2.82 against an estimate of 2.16 [D1]. Net income of 397 million rose 107.85 percent from a year earlier and earnings per share rose 63.95 percent, both faster than the revenue growth of 36.54 percent, so profit ran well ahead of sales [D1]. Communications Solutions Group revenue of 1.35 billion grew 43.09 percent and its operating income of 458 million grew 86.18 percent, while Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue of 501 million grew 21.60 percent and its operating income of 155 million grew 68.48 percent [D1]. Aggregate segment operating income of 613 million grew 81.36 percent, so the operating leverage is broad rather than confined to one line [D1]. Orders rose sharply to a second consecutive record, and the company guided the fourth quarter to revenue of 1.93 billion to 1.95 billion and earnings per share of 3.34 to 3.40 on a diluted share count of 172 million [D1].

Management said the quarter was another record with broad-based growth across its markets, with orders, revenue and earnings per share all up sharply and the outlook raised for the fourth quarter and the full fiscal year [D3]. Management attributed that momentum to rapid scaling of the artificial intelligence infrastructure ecosystem and said wireline orders more than doubled from a year earlier [D3]. Wireline revenue passed wireless revenue for the first time as demand for higher-speed optical transceivers in AI data centres grew, with the communications segment supplying the bulk of the growth [D2]. Management said demand is far exceeding its ability to supply and that the order funnel stands at an all-time high, so revenue is still to be converted in coming quarters [D4]. Management also said the 6G opportunity is likely to be larger than the 5G cycle, with customers moving into funded development programmes [D4].

The shares fell 6.32 percent in the session on 2026-08-19 even though earnings per share of 2.82 beat the estimate of 2.16 by 30.56 percent, which is the tension the market is working through [D1]. The fourth-quarter guidance range sits only modestly above the revenue just reported, and analysts questioned that modest sequential step and pressed for colour on the year that follows [D3]. Management said supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue for the next several quarters and that the supply situation is likely to be nonlinear, so booked demand may reach the income statement later than the market expects [D3]. Management also cautioned that one-time tariff impacts lifted fiscal 2026 profitability and will not repeat, which raises the bar the following year has to clear [D3]. Selling, general and administrative expense grew 25.99 percent and research and development expense grew 24.80 percent, so the cost base is expanding quickly and a revenue shortfall would press on margins [D1].

The shares trade at a trailing price to earnings of 45.89 against a forward figure of 20.66, so much of the guided step-up is already in the price [D1]. The writer of the price target piece argues that upward revisions to the earnings estimate and a top-ranked score point to further upside, while cautioning that analyst price targets mislead investors more often than they guide [D5]. An opinion piece linked from the call coverage argues that the AI growth is strong but that the valuation leaves little room for error [D3]. Management will take part in upcoming investor conferences, which puts its account of AI demand and supply conversion in front of investors before the next report [D6].
